sources.citation: Abbott, Stan. 1985. Nor-Pondo lexicostatistical survey. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 22 (Pacific Linguistics A-63), 313-338. DOI 10.15144/PL-A63.313.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No prose statement. Appendix B (pp.329ff.) gives diagnostic wordlists for four Angoram villages (Kambrindo, Marbuk, Magendo 2, Kanduanam) in phonetic transcription with a stress mark (raised apostrophe) before the stressed syllable, e.g. 'phondo 'man', 'khapan 'big', 'khambwakh 'stone' -- raw stress-marked data only.

sources.citation: Laycock, Donald C. & John Z'graggen. 1975. The Sepik-Ramu phylum. In S.A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1: Papuan languages and the New Guinea linguistic scene (Pacific Linguistics C-38), 731-763. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only a phylum-wide typological remark, p.732: among features 'widespread throughout the phylum.. lack of complex suprasegmental systems'. The Pondo-family section (pp.753-756) sketches Chambri phonemes/morphology with passing remarks on Angoram object marking; nothing on Angoram stress.
